title: Why Eval++ Is the Next Great Compute Primitive — Sunil Pai & Matt Carey, Cloudflare

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 76%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk presents Cloudflare's Durable Objects, Agents SDK, and Dynamic Workers as platform primitives that developers build AI agents on, fitting the 'substrate other engineers use' criterion. Primary audience is software builders on Cloudflare's developer platform, with a coding agent harness as a notable application being built on top. Durable Objects and Agents SDK are production-ready, while the coding agent harness is shipping imminently and M- CMS is in early preview. Prerequisites include familiarity with serverless, JavaScript isolates, MCP protocol, and capability-based security models. Conference presentation with on-screen API walkthroughs and audience Q&A. All evidence anchors are graded 'said_in_transcript' from the transcript.

summary: Matt Carey and Sunil Pai from Cloudflare's agents team introduce Durable Objects as the solution to serverless's fundamental statelessness problem: a class that spins up once per ID and routes all future requests and WebSocket connections to the same instance. At ~15ms London latency—faster than a single 16ms animation frame at 60 FPS—this enables real-time multi-device sync. Durable Objects are addressable, persistent, hibernating, and capable of long-running background work, making them the ideal compute unit for AI agents. The Agents SDK extends this with scheduling, callable methods, React hooks, plain JS clients, and scales to millions or trillions of instances. Cloudflare built a first-class backend for Vercel's AI SDK handling tool calls, synchronization, resumability, and multi-tab sync. Resumable streaming works by simply reconnecting to the Durable Object, which continues delivering the stream; multi-tab and multi-device sync come automatically. The speakers argue AI should be multiplayer, noting ChatGPT still cannot share a conversation link for collaborative use, while Durable Objects make this trivial without userland distributed systems engineering. The major reveal is Dynamic Workers: pass a string of LLM- or user-generated code and it runs in an isolated worker with zero ambient access—no fetch, no APIs, no env vars—with capabilities explicitly granted from outside. This inverts the VM/container security model and is framed as 'eval plus plus,' reclaiming 30 years of avoided eval. They give the example of generative UI: instead of generating JSON to render, Dynamic Workers let agents generate and render HTML or React directly in a safe sandbox. The speakers confirm they are building a coding agent harness entirely on Workers, shipping imminently, with persistent state connectable from any client. Storage includes SQLite directly in Durable Objects, R2 for larger files, and @cloudflare/shell providing a full virtual file system. JavaScript and Python are first-class; other languages run via WASM, with Zig experiments yielding tiny bundles. They mention M-, a CMS whose plugin system runs on Dynamic Workers, and tease upcoming talks on collapsing 2,600 Cloudflare API endpoints into a 1,000-token MCP tool. They close by inviting attendees to their expo booth, their talks (5:40 p.m. today and tomorrow), and sharing documentation at agents.cloudflare.com and issues at github.com/cloudflareagents.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Durable Objects are Cloudflare's stateful serverless primitive: a class that spins up once per ID, routing all future requests to the same instance, enabling persistence, hibernation, and background execution.

Resumable streaming with Durable Objects requires only reconnection—the stream continues automatically—and multi-tab/multi-device sync comes out of the box without userland distributed systems engineering.
Dynamic Workers run LLM- or user-generated code strings in sandboxed isolates with zero ambient access; capabilities are explicitly granted from outside, inverting the VM security model.
Dynamic Workers enable generative UI where agents generate and render HTML or React directly in a safe sandbox, instead of generating JSON intermediaries.
The speakers confirm they are building a coding agent harness entirely on Workers, shipping imminently, with persistent state connectable from any client type.
Storage options include SQLite directly in Durable Objects, R2 for larger files, and @cloudflare/shell providing a full virtual file system layered on both, usable today.
M- is a new CMS with a plugin system built on Dynamic Workers for sandboxed execution, deployable on any platform, not just Cloudflare.
An upcoming talk demonstrates collapsing 2,600 Cloudflare API endpoints into a 1,000-token MCP tool using code mode.
Documentation is available at agents.cloudflare.com or developers.cloudflare.com/agents, with issues filable at github.com/cloudflareagents.

sections.title: Introductions and team context
sections.summary: Matt and Sunil introduce themselves from Cloudflare's agents team, based mostly in London. They've been building AI agents seriously for over a year with strong results, starting with Durable Objects.

sections.title: Durable Objects as stateful serverless
sections.summary: Explains the core problem: serverless functions spin up, handle a request, and lose all state. Durable Objects solve this by spinning up once per ID and routing all future requests to the same instance. Achieves ~15ms London latency, faster than a single 16ms animation frame, enabling real-time sync as demonstrated by TLDraw. Properties: addressable, persistent, hibernating, long-running background execution, and connectable.

sections.title: Agents SDK overview
sections.summary: The Agents SDK lets you import from agents, extend a class, define callables from clients, and schedule background tasks. Provides React hooks and plain JS clients. Scales to millions or trillions of instances.

sections.title: AI SDK backend and MCP servers
sections.summary: Cloudflare built a first-class backend for Vercel's AI SDK, handling production concerns like tool calls, synchronization, resumability, and multi-tab sync. Durable Objects turned out to be excellent for MCP servers because they maintain stateful connections easily. Early MCP server adopters include PayPal, Sentry, Linear, and Intercom.

sections.title: Dynamic Workers reveal
sections.summary: Introduces Dynamic Workers: run a string of LLM- or user-generated code in its own isolated worker without deploying. Security model inverts the VM approach: starts with zero access and you explicitly grant only needed capabilities. Not a full VM—lightweight isolate, billions on demand. Replaces DSLs with actual code. Framed as 'eval plus plus' reclaiming 30 years of avoided eval.

sections.title: Talk teasers and audience Q&A start
sections.summary: Teases upcoming talks: one at 5:40pm on code mode, collapsing 2,600 Cloudflare API endpoints into a 1,000-token MCP tool. Both speakers claim to have fixed MCP twice. Audience member begins asking about mapping all the concepts together.

sections.title: Generative UI and resumable streaming examples
sections.summary: Audience asks what people are building wrong. Sunil gives the generative UI example: people generate JSON to render instead of generating HTML or React directly, because platforms lack a primitive to render untrusted code—Dynamic Workers solve this. Matt explains resumable streaming: in serverless you need databases, replication, sticky sessions; with Durable Objects you reconnect and the stream continues automatically. Multi-tab and multi-device sync come out of the box. Argues AI should be multiplayer—ChatGPT still can't share conversation links for collaborative use.

sections.title: Coding agent harness and client connectivity
sections.summary: The speakers begin leaking that they are building a coding agent harness entirely on Workers, shipping imminently. The persistent Durable Object backend can be connected from any client—terminal, chat, phone, iOS app, web app—with full sync, resumability, and statefulness. They mention delegating to containers or browser sandboxes (Daytona, browser use) as needed, with Workers as the nexus connecting everything.

sections.title: Storage, language support, and tooling
sections.summary: Storage includes SQLite directly in Durable Objects, R2 for larger files, and @cloudflare/shell (usable today) providing a full virtual file system layered on both. JavaScript and Python are first-class; other languages run via WASM, with Zig experiments yielding tiny bundles compared to Go and Rust. worker-bundler runs a bundler inside a Worker, pulling NPM dependencies through Cloudflare cache instead of relying on NPM uptime.

sections.title: M- CMS, We Next, Agents Week, and pricing
sections.summary: Reveals M-, a new CMS running fully on Workers/Durable Objects with a plugin system built on Dynamic Workers for sandboxed security, deployable on any platform. Mentions We Next, a version of Next.js running fully on Workers. Teases an upcoming Agents Week with major announcements. Explains Cloudflare's low pricing stems from installing hardware near ISPs and buying bandwidth in bulk, so free accounts aren't marketing expenditure. Offers free credits to attendees.

sections.title: Closing remarks and resources
sections.summary: Speakers wrap up at time, apologize for running over, and invite attendees to visit their booth on the expo floor. One speaks at 5:40 p.m. today, the other tomorrow. They share documentation links (agents.cloudflare.com or developers.cloudflare.com/agents), the GitHub repo (github.com/cloudflareagents) for filing issues, and express enthusiasm for chatting with attendees and seeing what people build.
